clue.text: Bet on team which is bottom

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A punter backs a team that is stuck at the bottom of the league.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is an informal word for the buttocks, which a person's bottom also names.

clue.text: Party admitting northern Ireland exile

indicators.note: admitting means the party word lets the next letters in

parts.note: a bash is a party
I is the abbreviation for Ireland

explanation.surface: A political party lets in a Northern Irish expatriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' reads as a political party, chiming with Northern Ireland, but it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to send them away, to exile them.

clue.text: Sleep around raising gasp

parts.note: CA, circa, means around

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, turns the word for gasp upwards

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps around, causing gasps of scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep around' reads as promiscuity; it splits into the definition and the abbreviation CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep or doze.

clue.text: Struggle with Sunday express?

parts.note: an express is a fast train

explanation.surface: Battling with the Sunday Express newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday express' suggests the newspaper; the question mark warns that express is a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to make a great effort, to struggle.

clue.text: Batman appears after policeman's confused

indicators.note: appears after means the batman word follows the policeman

parts.note: a DI, Detective Inspector, is a policeman; with the 's this gives DIS
a batman is an officer's servant in the army, an orderly

explanation.surface: Batman shows up after a bewildered police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batman' suggests the superhero; it is an army officer's servant, also called an orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means untidy and jumbled, a muddled or confused state.

clue.text: Bachelor boys embracing sweetheart?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in a degree

indicators.note: embracing means the word for boys wraps around the next letter

parts.note: lads are boys
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Unmarried young men cuddle up to a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: blades are dashing young men about town, the kind of bachelors who go courting.
explanation.definitionFit: Blade is an old slang term for a dashing, fashionable young man.

clue.text: Naked, we hear, on the beach

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: naked can mean plain and unadorned, as literal truth is

explanation.surface: Word gets round that people are nude on the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' with 'beach' paints nudists, but naked means plain, unembellished, as in the naked or literal truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral describes the shore zone, things found on or by the beach.

clue.text: Sophisticated young lady's ecstatic

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young lady entering society
on air is an idiom for being elated, walking on air

explanation.surface: A society girl is thrilled and polished.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and stylishly charming.

clue.text: Piercing whistle catching fruit

indicators.note: catching means the word for whistle holds the fruit inside

parts.note: a kettle or the wind sings when it whistles
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A shrill whistle as a fruit is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' looks like a description of the whistle; it is the definition, stabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearing something is stabbing it through, piercing it.

clue.text: Practice of topless tart minus clobber!

indicators.note: to clobber is to batter, so these letters are knocked into a new order
topless means the word tart loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A risque tale of a scantily clad woman who has shed her clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' looks like the noun for clothes, but it is the verb, signalling an anagram of ART (tart without its first letter) plus MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism, going about unclothed, is a lifestyle or habit one follows, hence a practice.

clue.text: Good man's fit and strong

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A decent fellow is healthy and robust.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means firm and steady, as a strong structure is.

clue.text: Man from Pamplona and Paris, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of these words might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A traveller hails from both a Spanish city and the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamplona is a city in Spain, so a man from there is a native of Spain.

clue.text: Trap care of queen taking rook and knight

parts.note: C/O, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A chess game where the queen captures a rook and a knight to trap the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap them with no way out.

clue.text: Works canteens containing useless food

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the next ones
works signals the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: US, short for unserviceable, is crossword shorthand for useless

explanation.surface: Factory canteens serve inedible fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works canteens' reads as factory dining rooms, but 'Works' is the verb signalling a rearrangement; US for useless is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustenance is nourishment, what sustains the body.

clue.text: Name of English plant in allotment

indicators.note: in means the following letters sit inside the word for allotment

parts.note: a ration is an allotted share
to plant something is to put it in place

explanation.surface: Naming an English plant growing in a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' suggests a garden plot, which fits 'plant'; here it is a share or ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is one's standing, the esteem others hold one in.

clue.text: Move to Iran perhaps, at regime change

indicators.note: change signals the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Relocating to Iran, perhaps, after the government is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle abroad, such as in Iran.

clue.text: Finish in debt giving bequest

parts.note: end means finish
owing money means being in debt

explanation.surface: A person dies in debt, yet still leaves a legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowing means providing a gift or fund, as a legacy does.

clue.text: Plain father's back with mother

indicators.note: back means the word for father is turned backwards

parts.note: pa is father; the 's is read as is
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: Dad's returned along with Mum, to everyone's view.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means clear and evident, plain to see.

clue.text: Put an e-mail out to find work

indicators.note: out signals these letters are thrown out of order and reset

explanation.surface: Instructions to send an e-mail to discover some employment.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate is to handle or operate something skilfully, to work it.

clue.text: Needle for a right idiot on heroin

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the following letters below heroin's letter

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A hypodermic for a complete fool who uses heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' suggests a syringe, matching heroin; it is the verb, to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke and pester them.

clue.text: Hold up from coach in derailment

indicators.note: from means the letters come out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A delay caused by a coach derailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinder is to delay or obstruct, holding something up.

clue.text: Got on, round about, and got on

indicators.note: round means the word for aged goes around the word for about

parts.note: to get on is to grow old, so got on means aged
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: People who got along, more or less, and then advanced in years.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'got on' takes two senses: getting along with someone, and getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on with someone is to see eye to eye, to be in accord.

clue.text: Round girl's shy inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for shy goes within the word for girl

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
to shy is to throw, and to lob is to throw high

explanation.surface: A plump young woman is described as bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' reads as timid, but it is the verb meaning to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means shaped like a globe, so spherical or round.

clue.text: Pressing — demanding, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: demanding something is requiring or needing it

explanation.surface: A matter is urgent and requires attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like urgent, chiming with 'demanding'; here it is literal pressing, as of dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Working dough with the hands involves repeatedly pressing it.

clue.text: Constellation circling edge of sun emerges

indicators.note: circling means the constellation's name goes around the next letter

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

indicators.note: the edge of the word sun is taken as its opening letter

explanation.surface: A star group rings the sun's rim and comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to come up or appear, as something emerges.

clue.text: Us led and managed to dislodge

indicators.note: managed suggests these letters are handled and arranged anew

explanation.surface: Our leader organised an operation to oust someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle is to throw a rider from the horse, dislodging them.

clue.text: Fraction of stature head to foot

indicators.note: head to foot means the leading letter goes down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: stature is height

explanation.surface: A small part of someone's tallness, measured from top to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to foot' reads as a full-length measurement; it moves HEIGHT's first letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is a fraction.

clue.text: Regular's confident in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in means the word for confident goes inside the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
sure means confident

explanation.surface: A pub regular is self-assured after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like a pub regular; it means steady and even, as a measured pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured rhythm is steady and even, so regular.
